title: Responses compatibility: message routing & function-call contract edge cases
creator: Connor Lee
description: Goal: Identify and remediate a set of subtle compatibility mismatches between Redwood's Responses translation layer and the OpenAI Responses API surface. Focus areas include streaming chunk boundaries and event semantics, function/tool-call argument typing and missing-argument behavior, structured-output schema enforcement and partial outputs, and propagation of metadata (message-level ids, role attribution, and timing) through the runtime. The ticket covers design, test harness additions, instrumentation, and a staged rollout plan with runtime feature flags.
acceptance_criteria: A translation spec that enumerates all observed behavioral deltas between Redwood Responses and OpenAI Responses for streaming events and function-call messages
Implementation of runtime translation hooks that normalize deltas without altering customer-visible payloads when not necessary
End-to-end test harness covering: multi-chunk streaming reassembly, interleaved tool-call + stream, and structured-output partial/invalid cases
Metrics and tracing added to observe: dropped events, remapped fields, latency added by translation, and rates of schema fallback
Canary rollout plan with feature-flagged translation enabled for 5% of hosted traffic and automated rollback on error-rate delta > 0.5%
progress_updates: 2026-03-05: Ticket created after QA regression surfaced — certain streaming events with 'tool_call' metadata were being emitted out-of-order when proxied through the responses adapter.

2026-03-07: Spike completed to reproduce out-of-order emission locally; root cause narrowed to the streaming parser consuming an extra newline in chunk boundary case which caused a delayed 'end_of_function' marker.

2026-03-09: Design sync with PM and Runtime leads (notes linked). Decided to implement a two-stage rewrite: (1) canonical event model internal to runtime, (2) deterministic emitters for each external API shape (OpenAI/Redwood).
2026-03-11: Implemented canonical event model and initial adapter for streaming events. Basic unit tests added for chunk reassembly. Observability hooks staged but not fully instrumented.

2026-03-13: Added function-call argument validation rules and fallback policy: when a required argument is missing in incoming OpenAI-style payload, create a structured 'missing_arg' warning event and route to a configured fallback schema instead of dropping the call. Pending integration tests.
decisions: Adopt a canonical internal event graph (message, token_delta, tool_call_start, tool_call_arg, tool_call_end, end_of_stream) to isolate external API mismatches.
Do not mutate user-provided structured output by default; instead emit a validation event and allow the consumer to opt-in to automatic correction via a per-route flag.
Function-call shape differences will be handled by a typed-mapper with explicit conversion rules; lossy conversions must produce an audit event and be configurable per-customer.
Streaming reassembly must be deterministic and preserve original chunking where possible; where re-chunking is necessary we will emit 'chunk_rechunked' trace events for debuggability.
notes_for_reviewers: Key risk: silent behavioral changes for existing customers if translation is too aggressive. Reviewers should verify the adapter behaves in opt-in mode and confirm canary rollback path.

Pay special attention to function-call conversions where OpenAI allows absent optional keys; we must ensure Redwood's stricter typing does not reject previously accepted calls without explicit opt-in.
Performance budget: translation should add <1.5ms median CPU overhead per request in the 95th percentile request path. Benchmarks expected in PR description.
